claim: PACAP global knockout mice have decreased fertility.
source: PACAP global knockout mice have decreased fertility and PACAP modulates LH release.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on PACAP knockout mice.

claim: PACAP modulates LH release.
source: PACAP global knockout mice have decreased fertility and PACAP modulates LH release.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on PACAP's effects on LH.

claim: PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus.
source: We demonstrate that PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to, and make direct contact with, kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate and AVPV/PeN nuclei and a subset of these neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing projections and contacts.

claim: PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to kisspeptin neurons in the AVPV/PeN nuclei.
source: We demonstrate that PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to, and make direct contact with, kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate and AVPV/PeN nuclei and a subset of these neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing projections and contacts.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons make direct contact with kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus.
source: We demonstrate that PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to, and make direct contact with, kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate and AVPV/PeN nuclei and a subset of these neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing direct contacts.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons make direct contact with kisspeptin neurons in the AVPV/PeN nuclei.
source: We demonstrate that PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to, and make direct contact with, kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate and AVPV/PeN nuclei and a subset of these neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing direct contacts.

claim: A subset of kisspeptin neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
source: We demonstrate that PACAP-expressing neurons of the ventral premamillary nucleus of the hypothalamus (PMVPACAP) project to, and make direct contact with, kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate and AVPV/PeN nuclei and a subset of these neurons respond to PACAP exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre-injection led to delayed puberty onset in female mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the viral deletion studies.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset in female mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the genetic deletion studies.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre-injection led to impaired reproductive function in female mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the viral deletion studies.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to impaired reproductive function in female mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the genetic deletion studies.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV did not lead to delayed puberty onset in male mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no effect in males.

claim: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV did not lead to impaired reproductive function in male mice.
source: Targeted deletion of PACAP from the PMV through stereotaxic virally mediated cre- injection or genetic cross to LepR-i-cre mice with Adcyap1fl/fl mice led to delayed puberty onset and impaired reproductive function in female, but not male, mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no effect in males.

claim: Metabolic cues play a critical role in regulating puberty onset by modulating the release of kisspeptin and/or gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) at the hypothalamic level.
source: Metabolic cues play a critical role in this regulatory process by modulating the release of kisspeptin and/or gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) at the hypothalamic level (Navarro and Kaiser, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Situations of energy deficit cause fertility impairments through the suppression of pulsatile LH secretion.
source: Situations of energy deficit and surfeit are known to cause fertility impairments (e.g. hypothalamic amenorrhea in anorexia nervosa) through the suppression of pulsatile LH secretion, but the mechanism by which metabolic factors regulate gonadotrophic axis function is largely unknown (Laughlin et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Situations of energy surfeit cause fertility impairments through the suppression of pulsatile LH secretion.
source: Situations of energy deficit and surfeit are known to cause fertility impairments (e.g. hypothalamic amenorrhea in anorexia nervosa) through the suppression of pulsatile LH secretion, but the mechanism by which metabolic factors regulate gonadotrophic axis function is largely unknown (Laughlin et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Kisspeptins secreted from Kiss1 neurons in the arcuate nucleus are the main secretagogues of GnRH.
source: Kisspeptins, secreted from kisspeptin (Kiss1) neurons in the arcuate (ARC), anteroventral periventricular and periventricular (AVPV/PeN), are the main secretagogues of GnRH.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Kisspeptins secreted from Kiss1 neurons in the AVPV/PeN are the main secretagogues of GnRH.
source: Kisspeptins, secreted from kisspeptin (Kiss1) neurons in the arcuate (ARC), anteroventral periventricular and periventricular (AVPV/PeN), are the main secretagogues of GnRH.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Kiss1 neurons convey most of the regulatory cues of the gonadotropic axis.
source: Kiss1 neurons convey most of the regulatory cues of the gonadotropic axis, which determines the proper pulsatile or surge-like pattern of release of GnRH (Herbison, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Kiss1 neurons determine the proper pulsatile or surge-like pattern of release of GnRH.
source: Kiss1 neurons convey most of the regulatory cues of the gonadotropic axis, which determines the proper pulsatile or surge-like pattern of release of GnRH (Herbison, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PACAP has been implicated in central processes such as development of anxiety behavior.
source: PACAP has been implicated in central processes such as development of anxiety behavior (Mustafa, 2013) and circadian rhythms (Mertens et al., 2007) and, importantly, both the ligand and the receptor are present in a number of metabolic and reproductive nuclei in the hypothalamus, including the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) (Vaudry et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PACAP has been implicated in central processes such as circadian rhythms.
source: PACAP has been implicated in central processes such as development of anxiety behavior (Mustafa, 2013) and circadian rhythms (Mertens et al., 2007) and, importantly, both the ligand and the receptor are present in a number of metabolic and reproductive nuclei in the hypothalamus, including the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) (Vaudry et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PACAP ligand and receptor are present in a number of metabolic and reproductive nuclei in the hypothalamus, including the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH).
source: PACAP has been implicated in central processes such as development of anxiety behavior (Mustafa, 2013) and circadian rhythms (Mertens et al., 2007) and, importantly, both the ligand and the receptor are present in a number of metabolic and reproductive nuclei in the hypothalamus, including the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) (Vaudry et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The presence of PACAP in metabolic and reproductive nuclei has been linked to the anorectic action of leptin at the hypothalamic level by modulating the activity of POMC neurons directly.
source: The presence of PACAP in these nuclei has been linked to the anorectic action of leptin at the hypothalamic level by modulating the activity of POMC neurons directly (Hawke et al., 2009; Resch et al., 2013; Tanida et al., 2013; Martin et al., 2014; Mounien et al., 2006), but this has not been linked to its role in fertility.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Whole body deletion of PACAP signaling decreases fertility.
source: It is known that whole body deletion of PACAP signaling decreases fertility (Jamen et al., 2000) and central PACAP administration delays puberty onset in rodents (Szabó et al., 2002); however, its action on gonadotropin release remains controversial as both stimulatory and inhibitory actions have been reported in rodents after central PACAP infusion (Köves et al., 2014; Köves et al., 1998), indicating a degree of complexity that may be species- and/or sex-specific.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Central PACAP administration delays puberty onset in rodents.
source: It is known that whole body deletion of PACAP signaling decreases fertility (Jamen et al., 2000) and central PACAP administration delays puberty onset in rodents (Szabó et al., 2002); however, its action on gonadotropin release remains controversial as both stimulatory and inhibitory actions have been reported in rodents after central PACAP infusion (Köves et al., 2014; Köves et al., 1998), indicating a degree of complexity that may be species- and/or sex-specific.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Both stimulatory and inhibitory actions of PACAP on gonadotropin release have been reported in rodents after central PACAP infusion.
source: It is known that whole body deletion of PACAP signaling decreases fertility (Jamen et al., 2000) and central PACAP administration delays puberty onset in rodents (Szabó et al., 2002); however, its action on gonadotropin release remains controversial as both stimulatory and inhibitory actions have been reported in rodents after central PACAP infusion (Köves et al., 2014; Köves et al., 1998), indicating a degree of complexity that may be species- and/or sex-specific.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A number of studies have invoked PACAP in the metabolic role of leptin.
source: Interestingly, a number of studies have invoked PACAP in the metabolic role of leptin (Hawke et al., 2009; Tanida et al., 2013); however, whether this action is direct (PACAP released from leptin receptor (LepR) expressing neurons) or indirect remains to be determined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: LepR is expressed in a subset of kisspeptin neurons.
source: In the context of reproduction, while LepR is expressed in a subset of kisspeptin neurons (Smith et al., 2006), genetic studies have demonstrated that the main site of leptin's action to regulate reproduction is not on kisspeptin neurons directly, but rather through cells in the ventral premammillary nucleus (PMV) (Cavalcante et al., 2014; Donato et al., 2011; Donato et al., 2009; Cravo et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The main site of leptin's action to regulate reproduction is not on kisspeptin neurons directly, but rather through cells in the ventral premammillary nucleus (PMV).
source: In the context of reproduction, while LepR is expressed in a subset of kisspeptin neurons (Smith et al., 2006), genetic studies have demonstrated that the main site of leptin's action to regulate reproduction is not on kisspeptin neurons directly, but rather through cells in the ventral premammillary nucleus (PMV) (Cavalcante et al., 2014; Donato et al., 2011; Donato et al., 2009; Cravo et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PACAP is highly expressed in the PMV.
source: We observed that PACAP is highly expressed in this nucleus and therefore we sought to investigate if PACAP in the PMV is important in the regulation of reproductive function and whether it serves as a mediator of leptin to exert its reproductive role.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: The PMV is the region of the brain with the highest level of co-localization of pStat3 and PACAP.
source: We found that the PMV is the region of the brain with the highest level of co-localization of pStat3 (an indirect marker of LepR activity) and PACAP (Figure 1a); approximately 87% of the PACAP neurons also express pStat3 in that region, though only 70% of the LepR neurons co-express PACAP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Approximately 87% of the PACAP neurons also express pStat3 in the PMV.
source: We found that the PMV is the region of the brain with the highest level of co-localization of pStat3 (an indirect marker of LepR activity) and PACAP (Figure 1a); approximately 87% of the PACAP neurons also express pStat3 in that region, though only 70% of the LepR neurons co-express PACAP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Only 70% of the LepR neurons co-express PACAP in the PMV.
source: We found that the PMV is the region of the brain with the highest level of co-localization of pStat3 (an indirect marker of LepR activity) and PACAP (Figure 1a); approximately 87% of the PACAP neurons also express pStat3 in that region, though only 70% of the LepR neurons co-express PACAP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The central nucleus of the ventromedial hypothalamus shows co-localization of pStat3 and PACAP, although to a lesser extent than the PMV.
source: There are two other regions, both in the hypothalamus, that also show co-localization of pStat3 and PACAP, although to a lesser extent: the central nucleus of the ventromedial hypothalamus and the supramammillary nucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The supramammillary nucleus shows co-localization of pStat3 and PACAP, although to a lesser extent than the PMV.
source: There are two other regions, both in the hypothalamus, that also show co-localization of pStat3 and PACAP, although to a lesser extent: the central nucleus of the ventromedial hypothalamus and the supramammillary nucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females had delayed onset of puberty, measured by vaginal opening.
source: Compared to non-cre expressing littermate controls, LepR-i-cre; Adcyap1fl/fl females had delayed onset of puberty, measured both by vaginal opening and day of first estrus (Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b-d.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females had delayed onset of puberty, measured by day of first estrus.
source: Compared to non-cre expressing littermate controls, LepR-i-cre; Adcyap1fl/fl females had delayed onset of puberty, measured both by vaginal opening and day of first estrus (Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b-d.

claim: There was no significant change in body weight in LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals on regular chow or high fat diet.
source: There was no significant change in body weight in any of the animals on regular chow or high fat diet (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b.

claim: Deletion of PACAP from LepR neurons leads to dysregulated estrous cycling.
source: As expected, deletion of PACAP from LepR neurons leads to dysregulated estrous cycling (Figure 1e–g), though less markedly than the lesion of the PMV region (Donato et al., 2011); these LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females were able to get pregnant, but had fewer pups per litter (Figure 1h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e-g and citation to prior work.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females were able to get pregnant.
source: As expected, deletion of PACAP from LepR neurons leads to dysregulated estrous cycling (Figure 1e–g), though less markedly than the lesion of the PMV region (Donato et al., 2011); these LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females were able to get pregnant, but had fewer pups per litter (Figure 1h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1h.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females had fewer pups per litter.
source: As expected, deletion of PACAP from LepR neurons leads to dysregulated estrous cycling (Figure 1e–g), though less markedly than the lesion of the PMV region (Donato et al., 2011); these LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females were able to get pregnant, but had fewer pups per litter (Figure 1h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1h.

claim: All stages of follicle development were present in LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl females, including corpora lutea.
source: Consistent with the ability to become pregnant, all stages of follicle development were present, including corpora lutea (Figure 1—figure supplement 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3c.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals showed a blunted LH surge.
source: The LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals showed a blunted LH surge (Figure 1i), which correlates with the dysregulated estrous cycle (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1i.

claim: LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals had a blunted response to ovariectomy.
source: They also had a blunted response to ovariectomy and fewer pups per litter (Figure 1h,j).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1j.

claim: Kisspeptin administration led to a similar induction of LH in LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals and controls.
source: Kisspeptin administration led to a similar induction of LH in both groups (Figure 1k).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1k.

claim: GnRH neurons are able to respond normally to kisspeptin in LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals.
source: This provides further evidence that GnRH neurons are able to respond normally to kisspeptin and, therefore, the reproductive impairment observed in these mice must rely on, or relay through another neuron that stimulates kisspeptin release.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the kisspeptin administration experiment.

claim: Leptin administration to LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals after a fast induced a lower than expected rise in LH release.
source: Finally, leptin administration to these animals in the morning after a fast, induced a lower than expected rise in LH release (Figure 1l); by comparison to the littermate controls, the LH induction in response to leptin treatment was blunted by 30%.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1l.

claim: The LH induction in response to leptin treatment was blunted by 30% in LepR-i-cre;Adcyap1fl/fl animals compared to littermate controls.
source: Finally, leptin administration to these animals in the morning after a fast, induced a lower than expected rise in LH release (Figure 1l); by comparison to the littermate controls, the LH induction in response to leptin treatment was blunted by 30%.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1l.

claim: PACAP is responsible for transducing some, but not all, of the metabolic information relayed by leptin to the HPG axis.
source: This indicates that PACAP is responsible for transducing some, but not all, of the metabolic information relayed by leptin to the HPG axis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the leptin administration experiment showing partial blunting of LH response.

claim: Validated PMVPACAP knockout (KO) mice had marked dysregulation of the normal estrous cycle compared to littermate controls injected with a control virus.
source: We again found marked dysregulation of the normal estrous cycle when validated PMVPACAP knockout (KO) mice were compared to littermate controls injected with a control virus (same serotype without cre, Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Mice lacking PACAP in the PMV had fewer estrous cycles in a 25 day period.
source: Mice lacking PACAP in the PMV had fewer estrous cycles in a 25 day period and resultant longer cycle lengths (Figure 2d,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d,e.

claim: Mice lacking PACAP in the PMV had longer cycle lengths.
source: Mice lacking PACAP in the PMV had fewer estrous cycles in a 25 day period and resultant longer cycle lengths (Figure 2d,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d,e.

claim: PMVPACAP KO animals maintained equivalent body weight to control animals throughout the study.
source: To note, PMVPACAP KO animals maintained equivalent body weight to control animals throughout the study (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Nearly all control mice became pregnant and successfully produced litters within 21 days of mating.
source: Nearly all control mice became pregnant and successfully produced litters within 21 days of mating, indicating successful copulation on the first day of mating to the male.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the mating study.

claim: PMVPACAP KO mice had reduced fecundity, with decreased capacity to produce a litter after mating.
source: In contrast, the PMVPACAP KO mice had reduced fecundity, with decreased capacity to produce a litter after mating, and significant delay in the time to become pregnant (Figure 2f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: PMVPACAP KO mice had significant delay in the time to become pregnant.
source: In contrast, the PMVPACAP KO mice had reduced fecundity, with decreased capacity to produce a litter after mating, and significant delay in the time to become pregnant (Figure 2f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Pups produced by the PMVPACAP KO females did not survive more than one day post partum.
source: Furthermore, those pups that were produced by the PMVPACAP KO females did not survive more than one day post partum (data not shown), which was thought to be due to neglect/infanticide by the dam based on observation of the animals in their home cages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: There was a decrease in the number of corpora lutea in PMVPACAP KO mice.
source: Though we could not assess the litter size, we observed a decrease in the number of corpora lutea in these mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b), which suggests an impairment in ovulation, consistent with a smaller number of follicles maturing per cycle, as a consequence of reduced gonadotropins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: In control-injected animals the increase in LH between baseline (10:00) and surge (19:00) is significant.
source: In control-injected animals the increase in LH between baseline (10:00) and surge (19:00) is significant, whereas for the KO animals only a trend to increased LH was observed at 19:00, suggesting an alteration in the ability of these mice to mount a normal ovulatory LH surge (Figure 2g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: For the PMVPACAP KO animals only a trend to increased LH was observed at 19:00.
source: In control-injected animals the increase in LH between baseline (10:00) and surge (19:00) is significant, whereas for the KO animals only a trend to increased LH was observed at 19:00, suggesting an alteration in the ability of these mice to mount a normal ovulatory LH surge (Figure 2g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: The compensatory rise in LH after ovariectomy was not different between PMVPACAP KO and control groups.
source: On the other hand, the compensatory rise in LH after ovariectomy was not different between the two groups (Figure 2h), indicating that the circuitry downstream of gonadal feedback, particularly the ARCkisspeptin population, responds normally to the absence of sex steroids.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: PMVPACAP KO mice had a normal response to kisspeptin administration.
source: Similar to what we observed in response to kisspeptin administration in the LepR-i-cre; Adcyap1fl/fl ablated mice, PMVPACAP KO mice had a normal response to kisspeptin administration (Figure 2i), indicating intact signaling between kisspeptin and GnRH neurons, and supporting a role for PACAP to modulate kisspeptin release.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2i.

claim: The LH response to leptin administration after fasting was not reduced in PMVPACAP KO mice, instead there was a slight but significant increase in LH induction by leptin treatment.
source: Unexpectedly, the LH response was not reduced, instead there was a slight but significant increase in LH induction by leptin treatment (Figure 3j).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2j (note: text says Figure 3j but should be 2j based on context).

claim: PACAP from the PMV is necessary for normal reproductive function.
source: Overall these data show that PACAP from the PMV is necessary for normal reproductive function but not for the relay of leptin signal from this nucleus.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reproductive impairments in PMVPACAP KO mice.

claim: PACAP from the PMV is not necessary for the relay of leptin signal from this nucleus.
source: Overall these data show that PACAP from the PMV is necessary for normal reproductive function but not for the relay of leptin signal from this nucleus.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing normal or enhanced LH response to leptin in PMVPACAP KO mice.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons send projections to the AVPV/PeN kisspeptin neuron populations.
source: PMVPACAP neurons send projections to both regions of kisspeptin neuron populations, the AVPV/PeN and the ARC (Figure 3a,b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a,b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons send projections to the ARC kisspeptin neuron populations.
source: PMVPACAP neurons send projections to both regions of kisspeptin neuron populations, the AVPV/PeN and the ARC (Figure 3a,b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a,b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons are glutamatergic.
source: These PMVPACAP neurons are glutamatergic (Figure 3c), though there are also PMV glutamatergic neurons that do not express PACAP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: There are PMV glutamatergic neurons that do not express PACAP.
source: These PMVPACAP neurons are glutamatergic (Figure 3c), though there are also PMV glutamatergic neurons that do not express PACAP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: In the ARC, blue light stimulation of PMVPACAP neurons at regular intervals (1 s) in brain slices led to immediate (<6 ms latency) excitatory postsynaptic currents in kisspeptin neurons.
source: In the ARC, where kisspeptin neurons participate in the regulation of GnRH pulsatility (Clarkson et al., 2017), and the expression of the PACAP receptor has been demonstrated (Campbell et al., 2017), blue light stimulation of PMVPACAP neurons at regular intervals (1 s) in brain slices led to immediate (<6 ms latency) excitatory postsynaptic currents in kisspeptin neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping.

claim: There was a monosynaptic glutamatergic connection between PMVPACAP neurons and ARCkisspeptin neurons (14/19 kisspeptin neurons tested throughout the ARC).
source: In female mice (n = 5), there was a monosynaptic glutamatergic connection between PMVPACAP neurons and ARCkisspeptin neurons (14/19 kisspeptin neurons tested throughout the ARC), and this was less frequently observed in non-kisspeptin ARC neurons (only 5/17 neurons received direct monosynaptic input from PMVPACAP neurons) (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Only 5/17 non-kisspeptin ARC neurons received direct monosynaptic input from PMVPACAP neurons.
source: In female mice (n = 5), there was a monosynaptic glutamatergic connection between PMVPACAP neurons and ARCkisspeptin neurons (14/19 kisspeptin neurons tested throughout the ARC), and this was less frequently observed in non-kisspeptin ARC neurons (only 5/17 neurons received direct monosynaptic input from PMVPACAP neurons) (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The majority of AVPV/PeNkisspeptin neurons tested received direct input from PMVPACAP neurons (11/18 neurons connected).
source: Similarly, in the AVPV/PeN, where the kisspeptin neurons are thought to drive the large GnRH release that leads to the preovulatory LH surge (Herbison, 2016), the majority of AVPV/PeNkisspeptin neurons tested received direct input from PMVPACAP neurons (11/18 neurons connected) but only a small fraction of non-kisspeptin neurons assayed showed direct connectivity in response to activation of PMVPACAP neurons (2/13 neurons connected).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping.

claim: Only a small fraction of non-kisspeptin neurons in the AVPV/PeN showed direct connectivity in response to activation of PMVPACAP neurons (2/13 neurons connected).
source: Similarly, in the AVPV/PeN, where the kisspeptin neurons are thought to drive the large GnRH release that leads to the preovulatory LH surge (Herbison, 2016), the majority of AVPV/PeNkisspeptin neurons tested received direct input from PMVPACAP neurons (11/18 neurons connected) but only a small fraction of non-kisspeptin neurons assayed showed direct connectivity in response to activation of PMVPACAP neurons (2/13 neurons connected).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping.

claim: Nine AVPV/PeNkisspeptin cells (25%) exhibited increases in the numbers of calcium fluctuations with, typically, no change in basal fluorescence in response to PACAP.
source: PACAP was found to induce different effects on the basal and spontaneous calcium fluctuations observed in 34 AVPV/PeNkisspeptin neurons (four slices from each of 4 diestrous mice). Nine cells (25%) exhibited increases in the numbers of calcium fluctuations with, typically, no change in basal fluorescence, ten cells (29%) showed decreases in basal levels as well as the numbers of calcium fluctuations, and 15 neurons (46%) showed no response to PACAP application (Figure 3f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: No cells in the rostral and middle ARC responded to PACAP.
source: PACAP was found to induce region-dependent effects on fluorescence levels in ARCkisspeptin neurons. A total of 27 rostral, 64 middle, and 68 caudal neurons (each from 4 slices from four diestrous mice) were tested. While no cells in the rostral and middle ARC responded to PACAP, 17/68 (25%) of caudal kisspeptin neurons exhibited increases in fluorescence levels during PACAP application, with a decrease to basal fluorescence upon washout (Figure 3h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3h.

claim: PMVPACAP neurons project directly to kisspeptin neurons.
source: Together, with the channelrhodopsin circuit mapping experiments, these findings indicate that PMVPACAP neurons project directly to kisspeptin neurons, but PACAP has direct stimulatory effect on a subpopulation of neurons located in the caudal aspect of the ARC, and interspersed through the AVPV/PeN.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the channelrhodopsin circuit mapping and calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Deletion of PACAP from the PMV of adult female mice leads to >50% reduction in fecundity.
source: The most striking finding is that deletion of PACAP from the PMV of adult female mice leads to >50% reduction in fecundity, a novel role for the neuromodulator specific to the PMV.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the fecundity studies.

claim: PACAP is critical for fertility in whole body animal knockouts.
source: Previous work has shown that PACAP is critical for fertility in whole body animal knockouts or in whole brain injection studies (Jamen et al., 2000; Köves et al., 2003; Shintani et al., 2003), but the mechanism and localization of action was unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Circulating levels of leptin are essential for gonadotropin release.

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Removal of PACAP from leptin-responsive neurons blunted the ability of exogenous leptin to increase LH levels after fasting.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the leptin administration studies.

claim: Deletion of PACAP from the PMV either through viral delivery of cre recombinase to Adcyap1fl/fl mice or through crossing with LepR-i-cre mice led to a blunted LH surge.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the deletion studies.
